events.title: Battle of Flodden
events.description: English forces under the Earl of Surrey decisively defeated the Scottish army of King James IV near Branxton in Northumberland. James IV was killed in the battle, along with many Scottish nobles, clergy, and thousands of soldiers.
events.significance: It was one of the bloodiest battles between England and Scotland and left Scotland with an infant king, James V, causing political instability for years.

events.title: Continental Congress Adopts the Name 'United States'
events.description: The Second Continental Congress formally resolved to replace the phrase 'United Colonies' with 'United States' in official documents, following the Declaration of Independence issued in July.
events.significance: The change established the official name of the new nation and reflected the colonies' assertion of themselves as sovereign states.

events.title: California Admitted as the 31st State
events.description: Following the Compromise of 1850, California was admitted to the Union as a free state, just two years after the Mexican-American War ended and amid the Gold Rush population boom.
events.significance: California's admission upset the balance between free and slave states and was a key element in the tense sectional compromise preceding the Civil War.

events.title: Founding of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea
events.description: Kim Il Sung proclaimed the establishment of North Korea in Pyongyang, following the creation of the Republic of Korea in the south less than a month earlier, after the division of the peninsula at the end of World War II.
events.significance: The formal division of Korea set the stage for the Korean War (1950-1953) and a lasting Cold War standoff that continues today.

events.title: Death of Mao Zedong
events.description: Mao Zedong, founder of the People's Republic of China and Chairman of the Communist Party, died in Beijing at age 82 after years of declining health.
events.significance: His death ended an era of Chinese history and led to a power struggle that concluded with the arrest of the Gang of Four and the rise of Deng Xiaoping's economic reforms.
